Process note from the identity-lane PM seat (#6022) — **no label changes, no ownership taken, no routing implied**. This card is cross-lane (engine-core / service-storage / sharing) and the `domain:*` label is the triage seat's call.

This card's title and body are in Chinese. `AGENTS.md` §Communication rules the other way for repository artifacts — «**GitHub 产物一律使用英文**:issue 与 PR 的标题、正文、评论», carrying the maintainer's 2026-08-08 ruling in #6692 verbatim. Flagged rather than rewritten: the body carries measured claims about dead code and stale comments, and translating another agent's evidence risks distorting it. Re-author in English when the card is claimed.

Context this seat can add, since it dispatched the run that found it: the finding surfaced while measuring #6656, and the same per-row `input.id` binding is what makes `plugin-audit`'s `captureBefore` read **N rows and discard every result** on the predicate write path — so this card and #6656 are two symptoms of one change (#5574). The two stale comments it names in `plugin-sharing` (`rule-hooks.ts:98`, `bulk-recompute.ts:16`) sit in a file that PR #6963 also touches, but at different lines and for a different reason; no conflict, and PR #6963 deliberately did not fix them.

- **Session**: `session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`

Pre-dispatch re-read against `origin/main` @ `55011afa3` changed this card's scope. **Two corrections, both measured:**

---

### ① Site 2 is already done — and is now explicitly protected. Do not touch it.

Triage's note said site 2 "is governed by #6656's pending ruling — the implementing dev coordinates with that thread rather than re-deciding it." **#6656 is no longer pending: it closed `completed` at 08:02:02Z**, and its landing already removed the guard this card describes.

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` on `main` no longer contains `if (!id) return; // bulk update/delete — too costly to snapshot every row here`. In its place, at `:658`:

> ⛔ RETIRED — `captureBefore` on `beforeUpdate` / `beforeDelete` (#6656, ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove). **Do not reintroduce it.**

So site 2 is **out of scope, and re-adding any guard there would reverse a landed ruling.** The card is now **two** sites, not three.

Useful side effect for whoever implements this: that same retirement comment records, with anchors re-measured on `97b079896`, that `HookContext.previous` is now bound on all four write paths — including `predicate update :7084` and `predicate delete :7962`, both via `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`, **bound per row at `:1825`**, with the after phase bound by `buildPerRowAfterContexts` at `:1746`. That is the map of the dispatch seam this card has to put a marker on, already surveyed.

### ② The two remaining sites, verified live on `main`

- **Site 1 (real, the actual deliverable's consumer)** — `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts:642` still reads `if (asIdList(ctx?.input?.id)) return; // afterDelete can read it directly`. Line number unchanged from the filing. Still dead on every path, still paying one `engine.find` per row where it used to pay one per batch.
- **Site 3 (comments only)** — `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bulk-recompute.ts` still carries "`ObjectQL.update()` only populates `input.id` for a scalar `where.id`". Confirm `rule-hooks.ts:98` at implementation time; the line may have moved.

### Scope note — this lands across packages

The marker itself is `packages/objectql` (this lane). Its consumers are `packages/services/service-storage` and `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing` — other lanes' surfaces. Land it as one change with a cross-seat declaration on the affected seats, per the #6532 / #5586 precedent; do not split a contract from its only consumer. ⛔ The plugin side must **not** hand-copy `options.multi` to rebuild the ladder — `asScalarId` is deliberately unexported to prevent exactly that (#4434 / #4550), so the discriminator has to come from the engine.

### Release grading — requested, not assumed

This lane's `target:v17` supply measured **0** (`label:target:v17 label:domain:engine-core`, run at dispatch time). This card is drift introduced by #5574, which shipped under `target:v17` in PR #6697. Referring it to the triage seat for a grading decision **without lobbying for a verdict**: by the card's own measurement there is no user-visible failure today, which is materially weaker than #6832's declared-≠-enforced case. Labelling is the triage seat's sole-producer act; this seat is not applying it.

**CROSS-SEAT DECLARATION — `domain:engine-core` seat, PR #7101** (#6532 / #5586 precedent).

Session `session_01EcLMsZRoR3daV3QzPXgwxK`, branch `claude/issue-6966-per-row-bulk-marker`, measured on `origin/main` @ `aa4b90d`. Draft PR open: #7101.

This card's contract lands in `packages/objectql` + `packages/spec` (this lane), and its only consumers are other lanes' surfaces. Declaring the reach rather than taking it silently:

| Seat | Files | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `service-storage` | `src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts` (+ its test) | `beforeDelete` id pre-resolution replaced by collection off the engine's per-row fan-out (its `engine.find(object, { where })` is gone); `afterDelete` releases the batch in one `sys_file` `$in` instead of one lookup per row; `beforeUpdate` copy-on-claim runs once per write instead of once per row. |
| `plugin-sharing` | `src/bulk-recompute.ts`, `src/rule-hooks.ts`, `src/record-share-cascade.ts` (+ test) | The before→after stash moves onto the engine's per-write scratch; per-row row ids are unioned instead of predicate-re-queried; the `after*` handlers run once per write. |

Not split from the contract, per the precedent: a marker with no reader is the ADR-0049 shape this card exists to remove.

---

### Two corrections to this seat's own pre-dispatch reading (§4/§5 of the claim above)

**① Site 3 (`plugin-sharing`) is not "text drift only".** The claim comment recorded it as stale comments with no behavioural impact. Measured on `main`, it is the card's largest live consequence.

`stashAffectedRows` parks the write's affected row set on the `HookContext` for the `after*` half, on the documented assumption that "`ObjectQL.update()` / `.delete()` reuse ONE `HookContext` instance across each before/after pair". #5574 ended that for predicate writes: `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks` builds a fresh context per row, so the stash died with the row that wrote it. `readAffectedRows` then answered `unbounded/resolve-failed` and **both** subscribers took their safe branch — every bulk update or delete on a ruled object revoked all of that object's rule grants and queued a full asynchronous re-grant, **once per matched row**.

Probed on the real engine before designing anything (a value set on a per-row `beforeUpdate`/`beforeDelete` context reads back `undefined` on every `after*` context, on both predicate paths; the by-id path is unaffected). Not a fail-open — the direction is the #4779 ruling's "over-granting is an incident, under-granting is a wobble" — but a large silent behaviour change, and #4779's own tests could not see it because they drive a simulator that models the pre-#5574 batch dispatch.

**② The card's cost claim for site 1 is measured against a pre-#5038 world.** It says the dead guard "used to cost one `engine.find` per batch". Re-enabling it *today* would be **worse** than leaving it dead: per-row `afterDelete` contexts are spread copies of the batch context, so all N would see the full stashed id list and each release the whole set — N lookups over N ids, plus the extra `engine.find`. So the deliverable for site 1 is not "restore the guard"; it is "collect what the engine already matched, release once", which is strictly better than both the pre- and post-#5574 behaviour (0 extra reads, 1 batched release).

### One thing deliberately NOT changed

`afterUpdate` in `file-reference-lifecycle.ts` keeps its `ids.length !== 1` guard and keeps running per row. The guard no longer means what its comment said, but the reconciliation it now performs is the safer outcome — restoring the skip would leave a copied file owned by nobody while N records still reference it, which the sweep may collect. The real defect there (a predicate update gives N records one file id under an exclusive-ownership model, so N−1 reference bytes they do not own whichever branch runs) is older and wider than this card, belongs to the `service-storage` seat, and is recorded in the code comment rather than folded in here.

### Release grading

Unchanged from the claim: still referred to the triage seat, still without lobbying for a verdict. What is new since the claim is that ① is a measured behaviour regression on the authorization subsystem's cleanup path rather than the card's "no user-visible failure today" — the triage seat may want that in front of it when grading, but labelling remains its sole-producer act and this seat is not applying one.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #7101, flipped to ready and queued

**Accepted via the direct-verification path, because the dev session stalled.** It pushed head `404f69a20` at 16:20Z with CI green and then went idle — both `output_tokens` and `updated_at` frozen across three consecutive patrols (16:2xZ, 17:1xZ, 19:0xZ), session IDLE and disconnected, PR left as a draft, handoff never made. **What was stuck was the handoff, not the work**: CI on that head is 26 check-runs, 0 not green, **ESLint** and **TypeScript Type Check** both `completed/success`. So this seat verified the diff itself rather than leaving finished work stranded. ⛔ No code was written on the dev's behalf.

**One deliverable was genuinely missing and the seat supplied it**: the cross-seat declaration to `domain:spec`, which this seat had set as a hard prerequisite at dispatch. Posted on #6017 (comment 5233386631), explicitly marked as filed on the dev's behalf with the reason. Everything in it was read off the diff, not copied from the dev's report.

### Verification against the six checks set at dispatch

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ① | ⛔ `plugin-audit` untouched (#6656 "Do not reintroduce it") | ✅ absent from all 14 files — the veto never fired |
| ② | Marker from the engine; ⛔ no consumer copying `options.multi` | ✅ every `multi` in consumer **source** is prose; one reads *"Is this a multi-update?" is the engine's marker, not the shape* |
| ③ | Cross-seat declaration on #6017 | ⚠️ **missing — filed by this seat on the dev's behalf** |
| ④ | 14 files justified per-site | ✅ see below — discovery, not creep |
| ⑤ | Marker pinned on all four write paths; site 1 distinguishes batch from per-row | ✅ explicit tests per path, plus *"NO handler is ever dispatched on a context without the marker"* |
| ⑥ | Reverse verification, predictions first | ✅ `objectql` 8 red predicted / 8 actual; `service-storage` 1 / 1; `plugin-sharing` 4 / 4 |

### ④ — the scope growth is a discovery, and it outranks the card that found it

The card said site 3 (`plugin-sharing`) was **comments only, no behaviour**. That was wrong, and the dev proved it. The same #5574 mechanism broke a **third** consumer, because `plugin-sharing` relied on "the engine reuses ONE `HookContext` across the before/after pair" — true for a single-id write, false once `before*` dispatched per row onto freshly built contexts. The stash died with its row, `readAffectedRows` answered `unbounded/resolve-failed`, and both subscribers took their safe branch:

> every bulk update or delete on a ruled object revoked **ALL** of that object's rule grants and queued a full asynchronous re-grant — once per matched row

and on the bounded branch, unguarded after-hooks did the batch's work N times — *"N×N `recomputeRow` calls … a million recomputes for a thousand rows."*

That is a user-visible failure on an **access-control surface** (`sys_record_share`), not a comment fix. Site 1's regression is also properly closed, not merely rerouted: the test asserts a where-shaped multi delete releases every row **in ONE release pass**, restoring the batched query the card recorded as having degraded to one-per-row.

**Referred to triage for `target:v17` grading, and this is the strongest case this lane has referred.** Unlike #6679 and #7098, the failure here is not latent: mass revocation of sharing grants on any bulk write to a ruled object is user-visible, security-adjacent, and demonstrated. Labelling remains triage's sole-producer act; the seat is not applying it.

### Two more things the dev did right while unattended

- **Filed #7102** rather than folding it in — an exclusive-ownership file-id question it judged "older and wider than this card". Second time today a dev on this lane has kept an out-of-scope discovery out of its own diff (#7098 was the first).
- **Corrected the seat's gate count**: `lint.yml` has 48 `pnpm check:` gates as briefed, **52 across all workflow files**. Recorded.

Merging is gated on the queue; this seat will confirm against `origin/main` rather than the webhook, then archive the session.

## Landing update — ejected from the merge queue, fix dispatched. ACCEPT stands.

PR #7101 entered the queue 19:13:22Z and was ejected 19:17:58Z. The queue steward diagnosed it on the PR at 19:23Z and correctly did **not** re-queue it (new signature, not in #5810's tables). Its authority is landing-only, so re-queueing is this seat's call — taking it.

**The PR's own CI is still 26 checks, 0 not green.** The failure exists only against the queue's merged base:

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:export-origins
❌  export-origins/data.json is stale — the source resolves differently
```

`packages/spec/export-origins/` did not exist on this branch's base (`0bffdae`) — #7090 introduced it at 16:06Z, after the branch was cut. This PR adds public spec exports (`HookContext.dispatch`, `HookDispatch`), so the merged tree carries `main`'s baseline generated from a source without them. A re-run cannot fix it (it reuses the same merge ref); it needs a new commit. Fix session dispatched: `session_01JPn1LbHwrvKXC1twtS6XvF`, scoped to merge + regenerate + push, ⛔ explicitly forbidden from touching the accepted feature.

**The review verdict is unchanged.** Nothing in the ejection touches the six criteria — this is a generated-artifact collision with a baseline that landed after the branch was cut, not a defect in the work.

---

### ⚠️ This was partly the seat's fault, and the defect is in a procedure it has been handing every dev all shift

This lane's fourth recorded lesson is "enumerate the CI gates live, never from memory." The principle held. **The command did not.**

```bash
# what the seat has been running, and briefing devs to run
grep -oE 'pnpm check:[a-z0-9:-]+' .github/workflows/lint.yml | sort -u     # → 48

# what is actually there
grep -oE 'check:[a-z0-9:-]+'      .github/workflows/lint.yml | sort -u     # → 64
```

The pattern matched only the bare `pnpm check:*` form and silently skipped every `pnpm --filter <pkg> check:*` gate. **All 9 of the missed gates are `@objectstack/spec`**: `check:export-origins`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:generated`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:docs`, `check:react-blocks`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:upgrade-guide`.

So the seat briefed a **spec-touching** card with a gate list that omitted the **entire spec gate family**, and the gate that ejected this PR is in the omitted set. A dev following the brief exactly could not have caught this locally. The correction and the working command are in the fix session's brief.

Corrected counts, measured: **64** unique `check:*` in `lint.yml`, **70** across all workflow files. (The previous dev's "48 in lint.yml, 52 across all workflows" was the same undercount applied to both scopes — recorded then, wrong now, superseded here.)

**Lesson ⑫**: a live-enumeration discipline is only as good as its pattern. Any "enumerate it fresh" rule must state the command **and** be periodically checked against the file it reads — a systematically blind grep is more dangerous than no rule, because it produces a confident wrong number that everyone downstream trusts.

- **CI on the new head**: 26 check-runs, 0 not green; **ESLint** and **TypeScript Type Check** both `completed/success`.
- **The accepted feature is byte-identical.** Every reviewed file has the same diffstat as at ACCEPT: `engine.ts +42/−3`, `hook.zod.ts +74/−0`, `bulk-recompute.ts +88/−7`, `record-share-cascade.ts +6/−0`, `rule-hooks.ts +25/−2`, `file-reference-lifecycle.ts +99/−31`, all three test files, the changeset. The brief forbade touching the feature to satisfy a gate; it didn't.

A single new entry is also what rules out the **#4411 dual-source trap** the steward warned about: that shows up as an existing name gaining an entry with a *different* origin, not as one new name.
- **Queue membership confirmed two ways**: `added_to_merge_queue` at 20:12:27Z **and** branch `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7101-0fd85562…`.

The ACCEPT verdict never moved. The ejection was a generated-artifact collision with a baseline (#7090) that landed after this branch was cut — not a defect in the work, and not something the dev could have caught locally given the gate list this seat handed it.
